outcome.summary: No municipal naming, opening or dedication record was found in the swept corpus. The sweep found and visually checked a printed use of the road name on 1915-07-21, earlier than the 1915-11-22 observation already in the evidence file.

observations.publication: El Tiempo / The Times (San Juan, P.R.)
observations.printed_text: Mr. and Mrs. Walter Tischer will be at home to their friends after the fifteenth of August at 2 Mc Leary Avenue, a handsome concrete house which Mr. Tischer has just finished building as a present to his bride.
observations.typography_note: OCR reads 'Me'; the page image shows 'Mc'. The words are split across a line break as 'Mc' / 'Leary'.
observations.hash_scope: UFDC-served access derivatives retrieved 2026-11-03; not custodian archival master bytes and not the issue PDF.
observations.visual_check: Page header reads 'Wednesday July 21 1915' and page number '8'; passage read against the jp2 crop.
limits: Establishes printed use of the road name by 1915-07-21 only.
Does not establish a municipal naming act, opening, dedication or eponym.
Does not establish that '2 Mc Leary Avenue' is the same address as the 1915-11-22 'Avenida MacLeary. Parada 44' rental notice.

context_findings.finding: Justice James Harvey MacLeary of the Supreme Court of Porto Rico died on 5 January 1914; El Tiempo printed the news the same day.
sources: El Tiempo 1914-01-05, UFDC AA00096997/00920, page file 0080.txt
Boletín Mercantil de Puerto Rico 1914-01-07, p. 6, https://www.loc.gov/resource/sn91099739/1914-01-07/ed-1/?sp=6
context_findings.relevance: The death date matches the opening date of the naming-act gate window.

context_findings.finding: Contemporary social notes place the widow, Mrs. Mary King (M. K.) MacLeary, 'of the Condado' (1914-03-06) and at '13 Taft Ave.' (1915-03-19, 1915-05-30, 1915-07-10). Her house was named 'El Palmarito'. In May and July 1915 she advertised a bungalow/cottage on Taft Ave. for rent.
context_findings.relevance: The family lived and held rental property on Taft Avenue, which the 1916 evidence describes as the street McLeary leaves from.

context_findings.finding: The Boletín Mercantil obituary says one of the justice's daughters was staying 'en su residencia del Parque', and that his son Samuel H. MacLeary was an electrical engineer with the San Juan Light & Transit Co.
sources: Boletín Mercantil de Puerto Rico 1914-01-07, p. 6, https://www.loc.gov/resource/sn91099739/1914-01-07/ed-1/?sp=6
context_findings.relevance: OCR only and not visually checked. Which 'Parque' is meant is not established.

naming_mechanism_findings.finding: In 1915 El Tiempo's reports of San Juan Concejo Municipal sessions show the council accepting cessions of private streets in Santurce, sometimes naming them in the same act. This is the most likely route by which a private road such as McLeary became a named municipal street.

examples.text: Acepta el Concejo la cesión de terreno para una calle que será conocida por 'Calle Hermanas Látimer', Santurce ... luego de hecha la cesión según dispone la Ordenanza ...
Ordinance renaming calle O'Donnell to José Julián Acosta, approved unanimously; shows street naming by ordinance with signage ('letreros').
El Concejo Municipal ha aceptado el traspaso y cesión de la calle conocida por 'Avenida Nairu', en Santurce.
Se aceptó la cesión de la calle de Iturriaga, Santurce. Igualmente se aceptó otra calle cedida por el señor Avelino Vicente, en las cercanías del Hipódromo de Santurce.

naming_mechanism_findings.relevance: The naming act being sought may take the form of a council acceptance of a street cession rather than a naming ordinance.

naming_mechanism_findings.finding: Report of the ordinary council session of 30 June 1915: 'Fué acuerdo pasar al Ingeniero de la Ciudad y Comisión de Fomento un escrito cediendo una calle en Santurce.' The street is not named.

source.note: OCR misreads the year as 1916; the METS date is 1915-07-02, a Friday, matching the printed weekday.

naming_mechanism_findings.relevance: This falls three weeks before the first known printed use of 'Mc Leary Avenue' (1915-07-21). It is not identified as McLeary. The AGPR certification for this session (1915, box 110) should be checked.

naming_mechanism_findings.finding: Taft Avenue is already used as a street address by April 1914 ('5 Taft Ave., Ground floor, Stop 44, Santurce', 1914-04-22) and is described as 'between Dooley and Taft Avenues, Santurce' (1914-05-01).

hypotheses.statement: The road may be named for Justice James H. MacLeary (d. 1914-01-05) or for his family, who held property on Taft Avenue, either by a municipal act or by a private subdivision.
hypotheses.not_established_by: No naming record found; the name use, residence and death date are circumstantial only.

swept_corpus.source: UFDC per-page OCR, El Tiempo / The Times (San Juan), bibid AA00096997
swept_corpus.result: Name hits were reviewed by hand. Street-name use first appears 1915-07-21. No council, ordinance, naming, opening or dedication text naming McLeary was found. A second full-text pass searched council reports for street naming, cession and acceptance language; findings are under naming_mechanism_findings.
limits: El Tiempo does not report every council session or every agreement.

swept_corpus.source: Library of Congress Chronicling America per-page OCR, Boletín Mercantil de Puerto Rico, LCCN sn91099739
swept_corpus.range: All 399 LOC-held issues dated 1914-01-02 through 1915-04-30; LOC holds no issues of this title after 1915-04-30
swept_corpus.pattern: case-insensitive '(mac|mc|me|mae|mhe)\s*\.?\s*leary|l\s?eary'; second pass for street cession and renaming language
swept_corpus.result: All McLeary hits refer to the justice: Supreme Court memorial session and speeches (1914-01-13 to 1914-01-19) and the Hutchinson appointment to the vacancy (1914-05-19). Pitkin's speech (1914-01-17 p3) places the justice's house in Santurce. Other 'Leary' hits are passenger or guest lists and O'Leary citations. No street naming, cession or council text naming McLeary was found.
limits: 36 issues were not fully read because of LOC rate limits (listed in incomplete_issues).
LOC coverage ends 1915-04-30, before the 1915-06-30 cession lead and the 1915-07-21 first print use.
